5pct:
The Bachelor of Arts Legal Studies major at University of South Dakota, students will gain analytical, legal writing, research, advocacy and communication skills as they explore the relationship between law, society and individuals. This program is interdisciplinary, meaning students will graduate with a well-rounded understanding of the law through lenses such as history, business, communications and social justice. If students are specifically interested in pursuing a law degree, they'll find numerous opportunities to engage in pre-law activities and law school preparation. If students are interested in another path, their education will set them up for success in a wide range of graduate programs and careers.

Explore the history and impact of the law while expanding student's analytical, writing, advocacy and communication skills. A degree in legal studies will prepare them to enter law school or pursue a variety of careers, including those in the legal field.
5pe4: The Bachelor of Arts Sociology major at University of South Dakota, students will develop the quantitative, qualitative and problem-solving skills needed to critically think about and address society's challenges. Through classes that encourage students to be reflective and analytical, research opportunities mentored by faculty, and off-campus experiences like internships, students will come to better understand complex social dynamics in a wide variety of areas: family and marital change, religion, education, globalization, health care, crime, mass media, social movements and belief systems. Students will graduate from this program prepared for success in human and social services, public service and government, marketing, nonprofit development, law, journalism and business, among other fields. Also, the field of health care has increasingly focused on the social aspects of health and medicine, making an undergraduate sociology degree an excellent complement to pre-professional programs for medicine, public health, nursing and other health care fields.

In Bachelor of Business Administration - Health Services Administration major at University of South Dakota, students will learn to think creatively and collaborate effectively so they can develop the skills and gain the knowledge needed to manage health organizations. Here they will find a variety of experiential learning opportunities ranging from internships in Sioux Falls to study abroad trips to Japan.

The program prepares students for leadership roles in health care organizations by applying a comprehensive understanding of business to the ever-changing world of health care.
5pdb:
In the Bachelor of Business Administration in Marketing major at University of South Dakota, students will learn to think creatively and collaborate effectively so they can help customers solve problems. Here they will find a variety of experiential learning opportunities ranging from internships at Deloitte or KPMG to study abroad trips in Germany. This program provides them with rich experiences in and beyond the classroom so they can pursue their career in marketing.

A degree in marketing prepares students for a dynamic career field where they will understand consumer behavior, market strategy, market research and more.

Human factors professionals makes world run smoothly. Students will explore the interaction of humans and technology, testing the designs of systems, tasks, machines, tools and environments in order to enhance efficiency, ease of use, safety and productivity.

In Master of Arts - Psychology in Human Factors, student at University of South Dakota will conduct and administer applied psychological research and serve as human factors and ergonomics specialists for organizations such as the United States military, the Federal Aviation Administration, technology start-up firms, top companies such as Oracle and Microsoft, and universities including Michigan State and George Mason.

The University of South Dakota offers the state’s most comprehensive psychology program with graduate training leading to a Philosophy of Doctorate degree with specializations in clinical psychology or human factors. Clinical psychologists focus on rural communities, cross-cultural differences with a focus on Native Americans, disaster mental health, first aid, trauma and substance abuse. Human factors professionals explore the interaction of humans and technology, testing the designs of systems, tasks, machines, tools and environments. The program has been fully accredited by the American Psychology Association since 1971.

The Master of Science in Computer Science at University of South Dakota will prepare students to excel as a professional in the field. They will learn the ins and outs of the latest technological developments, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, pattern recognition, data science, information retrieval, internet of things, cybersecurity and big data. They will learn to apply their knowledge to solve real-world problems in every facet of society.

A master's degree in computer science prepares students for a career in any type of field as technology continues to shape the world. They will receive foundational knowledge that they can use to understand the complex problems of today and create the solutions of tomorrow. This program requires 30 credit hours and offers both a thesis and non-thesis track.

The business world is constantly changing and employers are seeking out leaders who have strong foundational knowledge in business concepts, critical thinking and problem solving. As a student in one of the top Master of Business Administration programs in the country they will be part of a program that emphasizes decision making, data analysis and social responsibility. They will learn from expert faculty who take a personalized approach to graduate students through one-on-one advising and support throughout their program.

The Master of Business Administration (MBA) program emphasizes analytical and critical thinking skills, evaluation of alternative courses of action, understanding of the impact of the business environment on business decisions and application of ethical principles in identifying and resolving business dilemmas.
